input: Open a joint bank account with my spouse

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether they want a checking account, savings account, or both determines which products to research and what steps are involved.
Whether they already bank at the same institution affects whether they open a new account together or add a joint holder to an existing one.
Whether they prefer to do this online, in a branch, or via a mobile app affects which banks are viable options and the required steps.
Minimum deposit requirements, monthly fees, or credit union membership eligibility could rule out certain banks entirely.
Their priorities — such as high interest rates, no fees, ATM access, or a specific bank's reputation — will guide which institution to recommend.
Understanding what they plan to use the account for (daily spending, shared bills, emergency fund, etc.) shapes which account type and features matter most.
Knowing what documents and ID both spouses currently have on hand determines how quickly they can proceed and what needs to be gathered first.

gold.taskTitle: Open a joint bank account with spouse
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to open a joint bank account together with their spouse, covering everything from choosing the right bank to completing the application.

questions.title: What type of account do you want to open?
questions.description: Is this a joint checking account for day-to-day spending, a joint savings account, or both? The account type determines which products to compare and what features to prioritize.

questions.title: Do you and your spouse already bank at the same place?
questions.description: If you share an existing bank, you may simply add a joint holder rather than starting from scratch. If you bank separately, you will need to choose a new institution together.

questions.title: Do you prefer to open the account online or in a branch?
questions.description: Some banks are online-only, while others require an in-person visit for joint accounts. Your preference narrows the field of eligible institutions significantly.

questions.title: Is there a budget for minimum deposits or monthly fees?
questions.description: Many joint accounts require an opening deposit or charge monthly maintenance fees unless a minimum balance is maintained. Knowing your limits rules out incompatible options early.

questions.title: What feature matters most to you in this account?
questions.description: For example: no monthly fees, a high interest rate, a large ATM network, strong mobile banking, or a bank you already trust. This guides which institution to recommend.

questions.title: What will this joint account mainly be used for?
questions.description: Whether it is for shared household bills, a vacation fund, an emergency fund, or everyday joint spending determines which account features and account type will serve you best.

questions.title: Do both spouses have valid government-issued ID ready?
questions.description: Most banks require both applicants to present a government ID, Social Security number, and proof of address. Knowing what you have on hand determines your immediate next step.
